solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'single, hurried paragraph' nearly restates 'abrupt'; distractors are not tempting
S022-01.notes: Long tension resolved in one hurried paragraph = abrupt. Inevitable/subtle/lavish don't fit the colon's explanation.

S022-02.notes: Six months while studying effects = provisional. Permanent contradicts; punitive/retroactive unsupported.

flags: minor: distractors C and D directly contradict or ignore the text; A is an unsupported superlative, so little challenge
S022-03.notes: Arms taste via suckers and respond before the brain fully processes the signal, so they act somewhat independently.

S022-04.notes: Pedestrian difference only in afternoon (hot), none in early morning, so shade appeals mainly in heat. B contradicted by morning data; C, D unsupported.

S022-05.notes: Need intermediate angle exceeding both extremes: 20° (480) > 0° (410) and 60° (380). A and B compare only partial pairs; D is a total. Arithmetic 410+480+455+380=1725 is correct.

S022-06.notes: Dangling modifier: the one who studied the ruins (the archaeologist) must immediately follow the comma. B, C, D put the date/founding/proposal as subject.

S022-07.notes: Inverted syntax; subject is plural 'two stone towers', so 'stand'. 'Stands'/'has stood' singular trap; 'standing' leaves no finite verb.

S022-08.notes: Second sentence adds another advantage (less energy) to the first (lower cost): 'Moreover'. Not contrast or example.

S022-09.notes: Only D states what the system was for (letting blind people read and write by touch).

S022-10.notes: Text explains light damage as reason the museum displays a replica and stores the original. B, C, D unsupported.
